clue.text: Sanitised account full of subtle spite

indicators.note: the abbreviation for account holds the shuffled letters inside it
subtle in the sense of crafty or intricate, so the word spite is worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An account of events has been cleaned up, yet still drips with understated malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subtle spite' reads as one phrase about the account, but 'subtle' is the anagram signal, making SEPTI, and 'full of' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free from germs has been sterilised, the same idea as sanitised.

clue.text: Each primate touring individual church

indicators.note: going round, so the ape encircles the single letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single individual
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Every ape travels around one particular church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals going round, not travel; 'individual' is the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: priced at a pound per item means each item costs that amount.

clue.text: Overlook tip of extremely cross-sounding waiters

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for the waiters gives the ending

parts.note: people waiting in line form queues

explanation.surface: Forgive the waiters who sound extremely annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-sounding' looks like one adjective, but cross is X and only 'waiters' is spoken: QUEUES pronounced gives CUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to pardon a fault is to let it pass unpunished, to overlook it.

clue.text: Shabby trio carrying plug and soap?

indicators.note: holding inside, so the word for trio contains the other pieces

parts.note: a trio is three
a plug is an advertisement, an AD
soap comes in a bar

explanation.surface: Three scruffy people are carrying a bath plug and some soap.
explanation.walkthrough: THREE carries AD and BAR: THRE(ADBAR)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn so thin the threads show is shabby.

clue.text: Finally found beneath tea leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter goes below the tea word

parts.note: char is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: At last someone found something lying under tea leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea leaves' looks like one thing; tea is CHAR and 'leaves' alone defines. D comes beneath CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a vegetable grown for its edible leaves.

clue.text: Scatter most of the crumbs

parts.note: to scatter is to strew

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An instruction to toss out nearly all the crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbs' is not bread but an exclamation of surprise; STREW plus TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise; strewth is chiefly Australian or British slang.

clue.text: Small particle of chromium oxide in rising cloud

indicators.note: placed inside the reversed cloud
in a down clue, going up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a nimbus is a rain cloud
Cr is the chemical symbol for chromium
O stands for oxygen, as in the oxide

explanation.surface: Specks of chromium oxide are carried up in a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NIMBUS into SUBMIN, and CR plus O goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something smaller than a micron, a millionth of a metre, so a tiny particle.

clue.text: Excellent case of Rioja leads to riotous evening

indicators.note: the outside letters of the wine name form its case
the leading letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A fine case of Spanish wine leads to a wild night.
explanation.walkthrough: RA from the outside of Rioja, then R and E leading riotous and evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: rare as a slangy word for splendid or first-rate.

clue.text: Endless conflict over fashionable drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second
the final letter is cut from the word for conflict

parts.note: warfare is armed conflict
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An endless war over some trendy narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the last letter; in a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfarin is an anticoagulant medicine, used to thin the blood.

clue.text: Shocked at these, I pause

indicators.note: shaken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Stunned by these things, I stop for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to waver or hold back briefly before acting is to pause.

clue.text: Contract eaten by dog?

parts.note: something eaten is in the animal
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A legal contract has been chewed up by the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is the verb, as in contracting a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to contract a debt or an illness is to bring it on oneself.

clue.text: Ms Rudd at last agreeing blubber constitutes whale product

parts.note: Amber Rudd, the British Conservative politician who was Home Secretary

indicators.note: the final letters of the next two words

parts.note: constitutes means is

explanation.surface: A politician finally concedes that blubber makes up a whale product.
explanation.walkthrough: Amber Rudd was UK Home Secretary when this ran. 'blubber' is not whale fat here, just a word giving its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance formed in sperm whales' intestines, prized in perfumery.

clue.text: Antics of Cupid stare one in the face

indicators.note: playful capers, so the letters cavort into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Cupid's playful stare is a slap in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in the face' is cryptic: the thing that lands in a clown's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick comedy: the gooey pie is thrown so that one lands in someone's face.

clue.text: Banks excluded from data legislation

indicators.note: banks are the edges, so the outer letters of the word for data go

parts.note: facts are data

explanation.surface: Banks are left out of data protection law.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by parliament is an act, a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Our lingo is rustic, like Gray's mute Milton

indicators.note: crude and rough, so the letters are roughed into a new order

explanation.surface: Our countryside dialect resembles the silent poet of Gray's Elegy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard imagines 'Some mute inglorious Milton' buried there; 'rustic' suits that churchyard scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary quotation: Gray's phrase describes an unknown, uncelebrated would-be poet.

clue.text: One who makes dim, daft subtractions

indicators.note: silly or crazy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dimwit who makes silly mistakes in arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim' looks like a description of the person, but it means obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person deliberately keeps things obscure, preventing knowledge from coming to light.

clue.text: Reprimand head of compliance over Italian wine scandal

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter sits above the next piece
the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: The compliance chief is told off over a scandal involving Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to castigate is to criticise or rebuke someone severely.

clue.text: Slow food in Melbourne's cargo terminal

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Some slow-arriving food is sitting in Melbourne's cargo terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow food' is a playful definition: snails are slow.
explanation.definitionFit: These are snails cooked as food, and snails are proverbially slow.

clue.text: Loyal Tory Unionist, twice and thrice over

indicators.note: going over the Unionist letter, the word for thrice surrounds it
the Unionist letter is used two times, once in each half

parts.note: treble means three times

explanation.surface: A loyal Conservative and Unionist, many times over.
explanation.walkthrough: TREBLE goes 'over' U 'twice', taking one in each half: TR(U)E BL(U)E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a staunch Conservative is called true blue, blue being the party's colour; generally it means steadfastly faithful.

clue.text: Unexpectedly morose guards quietly revolt

indicators.note: surrounds, so the sullen word encloses the others

parts.note: surly means morose
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a rising is a revolt

explanation.surface: Without warning, gloomy guards rise up in a quiet rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something done in a way that takes one aback happens unexpectedly.

clue.text: Are members of English Left enthralled by sound of Big Ben?

indicators.note: held captive inside the chime word

parts.note: the bell strikes with a bong

explanation.surface: Are English left-wingers spellbound by the chimes of Big Ben?
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell of the Houses of Parliament clock in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to belong to a club is to be one of its members.

clue.text: Floor of yard behind shop

indicators.note: the letter comes after the shop word

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: The floor of a yard at the back of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, a floor.

clue.text: Drink and be sick over the telephone

indicators.note: heard on the phone, so a word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Someone drinks and then is ill while on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is beer, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Burundi's barmen trying to comprehend legal ban

indicators.note: to include or hold within, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: Bartenders in Burundi trying to understand a legal ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck off as a barrister, expelled from the bar, is a ban imposed by legal authorities.

clue.text: Don't get out truncheon!

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batter who is not dismissed continues batting, two words
a police officer's stick or club

explanation.surface: A policeman warns someone not to pull out a club.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter who avoids being out bats on.
explanation.definitionFit: A police club is a stick also called a truncheon; the other sense is a cricket phrase.

clue.text: Vicious about AC/DC's last album?

indicators.note: turned round, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Sid Vicious was bassist of the Sex Pistols

indicators.note: the final letter of the band name

explanation.surface: Is the latest record by AC/DC aggressive?
explanation.walkthrough: SID backwards is DIS, then C.
explanation.definitionFit: A record released as an album is pressed on a disc.

clue.text: Gad about, dashing round eastern half of Kyiv

indicators.note: going round, so the adjective encloses the fragment

parts.note: gallant means dashing

indicators.note: the right-hand half of the city name, east on a map

explanation.surface: Someone dashes about Kyiv, wandering the eastern districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern half of' means the right-hand half of the written name, as east is right on a map; 'round' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to roam around seeking pleasure is to gad about.

clue.text: Bees leaving Bob with grim smell

indicators.note: departing, so those letters go from the name

parts.note: two letter B's, spelled out as bees
dour means grim

explanation.surface: The bees fly off, leaving Bob with a grim smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both B's from Bob leaves O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an odour is a smell, often an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Mawkishness of Malcolm periodically restrained by elder?

indicators.note: held within, so the tree word encloses the letters

parts.note: the elder is a tree

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: Malcolm's sentimentality is now and then held in check by an older relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' looks like an older person but is the tree; ACL from Malcolm goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: excessive sweet sentimentality, as cloying as syrup.

clue.text: Posy makes horse noise, according to Spooner

indicators.note: swapping the starting sounds, as Rev Spooner famously did

parts.note: to go is to make a noise, as in the cow goes moo
a horse neighs

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers makes a whinny, says Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a nosegay is a small bunch of flowers.
